text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
American cavalry commander GEORGE ARMSTRONG CUSTER, known for his "last stand" against the Cheyene and Sioux Indians, was born in 1839.
Irish/Australian explorer JOHN KING was born in 1841. He was the sole survivor of the BOURKE and WILLS expedition. Aborigines cared for him until he was rescued.
American pioneer of rock'n'roll LITTLE RICHARD, whose hits included "Tutti Frutti" and "Good Golly, Miss Molly", was born in 1935.
Australian entertainer DENISE DRYSDALE, who earned the unfortunate nickname of "Ding Dong", was born in 1938.

American guitarist, singer and songwriter J.J. CALE (JEAN JACQUES) was born in 1938. In 1965 he made his first album, which included the original version of "After Midnight". In 1966 he formed the 'Leathercoated Minds' and made one album. He didn't become a house-hold name until after ERIC CLAPTON had a hit with "After Midnight". Another hit was "Crazy Mama" in 1972. J.J. CALE has a cult following among those who have a taste for country-blues and excellent guitar playing.
Spanish operatic tenor JOSE CARRERAS, who overcame leukaemia to become one of opera's superstars, was born in 1946. He is one of the "Three Tenors" with PLACIDO DOMINGO and LUCIANO PAVAROTTI.

Canadian singer and songwriter ANDY KIM (ANDREW JOACHIM), who co-wrote "Sugar, Sugar", was born in 1946. He had hits with "Baby I Love You" (1969) and "Rock Mr Gently" (1974). He reappeared with a new album in 1983 under the name of BARRON LONGFELLOW.
American singer/songwriter JACK RUSSELL, who was with the group 'Great White', was born in 1960. Hits included "Once Bitten Twice Shy" (1989) and "The Angel" (1989).
** EVENTS **
1791 : WOLFGANG AMADEUS MOZART died in Vienna of kidney
failure. He was 35 and died a pauper. He wrote his first composition when he was five and wrote more than 600 works. Only the gravedigger attended his burial in a Viennese suburb.
1792 : GEORGE WASHINGTON was re-elected president of the
United States.
1870 : The author of "The Count of Monte Cristo" and "The
Musketeers", ALEXANDRE DUMAS, died.
1904 : The Japanese destroyed the Russian fleet at Port
Arthur.
1933 : The alcohol came out of the closet and flowed

freely as the United States celebrated the end of 14 long years of Prohibition. The "noble experiment", which was the result of campaigning by the Temperance Movement and the Women's Christian Temperance Union, was helped by the World War One grain shortage. It didn't work and drove the lucrative liquor trade into the hands of criminals like AL CAPONE. Enforcement proved difficult and unpopular with police.
1945 : Six United States navy aircraft carrying 27 airmen

went missing in the Atlantic near Bermuda, in an area that became known as the Bermuda Triangle. Five bombers took off from the Florida air base, Fort Lauderdale, for a training flight. A sixth plane was sent to look for the aircraft when radio contact was lost. It too lost radio contact and no trace was found of the six planes.
1944 : General PATTON's troops reached the Siegfried
Line.
1956 : ROSE HEILBRON became the first female judge in
Britain.
1964 : The break-away party from the ALP - the DLP, the
Democratic Labor Party won two Senate seats with VINCE GAIR and FRANK McMANUS being elected to the upper house.
1977 : President SADAT of Egypt severed links with Syria,
Libya, Algeria and South Yemen.
1978 : The USSR signed a 20-year treaty of fri*ndship
with Afghanistan.
1979 : A report released in Canberra revealed that one
million Australians, mostly married women, were working part time.
1987 : Britain's hole in the heart baby DAVID BARBER died
11 days after his operation.
